$comment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): every `*.format.json` now carries a `predefinedMacros` root key -- the C-visible face of that file's own `dataModel` -- merged with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, format-filtered exactly ONCE, and fatal on a name collision across ANY of the three families. This is the runnable end-to-end pin on every shipped (architecture x object-format) leg: preprocess -> parse -> lower -> codegen -> LINK -> spawn -> stdout + exit code. WHAT IT CLOSES, MEASURED before the change on arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-staticlib: `__arm64__` defined, `__APPLE__` defined, `__LP64__` NOT defined, yet sizeof(long)==8 and sizeof(void*)==8 -- LP64 widths compiled against ILP32 header arms. The macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16: sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. STRUCTURE: four independently falsifiable compile-time legs (the two spellings agree / the row's VALUE is 1 / the selected arm agrees with sizeof(long) and sizeof(void*) / the same coherence on a long-bearing AGGREGATE) plus a runtime arm that recomputes the widths through a real call boundary. Both routes are arithmetically compensated to exit 42 (8+8+26 == 4+8+30 == 42) BECAUSE THE POINT IS THAT A COHERENT WORLD EXITS 42 WHICHEVER DATA MODEL IT HAS -- so the exit code alone cannot tell the routes apart, and each route also `puts` a distinct tag pinned per target below. THAT tag is what proves the pe64 leg took the NEGATIVE arm instead of quietly taking the LP64 one. ★ WHY ALL FOUR TARGETS AND NOT ONLY MACHO (which the directory is named for -- it is named for the leg whose defect it closes, not for its coverage): the defect was FOUND on macho, but the REASON the channel lives on the OBJECT FORMAT rather than the target is the pe64 leg -- x86_64 is LP64 under elf64/macho64 and LLP64 under pe64, so the SAME CPU must answer differently. A macho-only example would stay green if a maintainer pasted the rows into pe64-*.format.json, which is the miscompile (Windows headers taking their LP64 arms against a 32-bit `long`) the format-layer decision exists to prevent. The pe64 leg therefore asserts __LP64__ is NOT defined and that `long` is 4 bytes, and exits 42 only if BOTH hold -- the stronger direction. CLANG GROUND TRUTH (MEASURED 2026-07-30, `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`, Apple clang 21.0.0): __LP64__ 1 AND _LP64 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; NEITHER on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- so the shipped LP64 formats and the shipped LLP64 formats each match clang exactly. `/usr/bin/clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` is CLEAN (rc 0) on arm64-apple-darwin and x86_64-apple-darwin with the real SDK, and (with `#include <stdio.h>` replaced by a `puts` prototype, since this host has no cross-SDK headers) also clean under aarch64-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu AND x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- i.e. clang's own data models satisfy every _Static_assert here, including the LLP64 one. The clang-built native binary on this arm64-darwin host prints `model=lp64` and exits 42, byte-for-byte what DSS produces for arm64:macho64.
